full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Mamtaz Uddin Ahmed J.:-Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners do form part of the main application. This is an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh challenging Judgment and Decree dated 05.07.2007 (degree signed on 11.07.2007) passed by the Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 480 of 2003, whereby the suit was decreased ex-parte against the defendant petitioners including defendant respondent nos. 3-6 and against the contesting added defendant No. 7 to the effect that: 

 2. Mr. S.N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the writ petitioner has taken us through the writ petition and the annexure to the writ petition and submits that the petitioners are guarantor of the loan granted to the borrower Sonargaon Dying process and Finishing Mills Ltd. represented by its Managing Director late Md. Akhtaruzzaman Khan and as such, according to Section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the mortgaged properties of the borrower requires to be sold first for the purpose of realization of the decrcetal money. He submits that the impugned auction notice (Annexure-B) itself shows that there are mortgage properties of the borrower himself and as such the inclusion of the mortgaged property of the writ petitioners in the auction notice before selling the mortgage properties of the borrower has submitted illegality. Mr. Goswami further submitted that no step has yet been taken to sell the mortgaged property of the borrower and as such, mortgaged properties of the borrower is required to be sold first for the purpose of realization of the decreetal amount according to Section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. It is further submitted that the decree holder after obtaining the preliminary decree dated 11.07.2007, started Artha Rin Zari case No.512 of 2008 and the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 in not giving effect to the provisions of Section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has passed the impugned order dated 18.06.2009 and as such the impugned auction notice is liable to be declared to have been published without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 4. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the learned D.A.G. and perused the writ petition and the Annexure to the writ petition. It has been found from the notice that no mortgaged property of the borrower has been included in the auction notice dated 09.07.2009 published in Daily Amar Desh by Sonali Bank, in. order to sell the mortgaged of the properties petitioners (Annexure B). Section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Ain clearly provides that the mortgage properties of the borrower requires to be sold first. for the purpose of realization of the decreetal money but the properties of the borrower has not been included in the auction notice and as such, the learned Artha Rin Adalat Judge has violated the specific provision of law and thus acted without lawful authority. On the face of the order, it arrears that the learned judge has committed an error of law and the order definitely has jeopardized the interest of the guarantor and as such, it appears to us the impugned order and the auction notice arc not sustainable in law and the same is liable to be declared to have passed without lawful authority. However, we are not inclined to issue rule for procedural mistake. The ends of Justice would be met if the impugned order is set aside and accordingly the impugned order and the auction notice are set aside and the Artha Rin Adalat is directed to follow the provisions of Section 6(5) of the Artha Rin Ain Strictly having regard to the provision of section 33 in its entirety in order to satisfy the decree.
